title: Case: Recipient reports a cracked lamp and asks whether her doorstep signature blocks a claim
context: A pair of ceramic table lamps from Quillmoor Goods arrived with one base cracked. Damage intake has logged the report and is waiting on the carrier's condition record.
initial_request: Any news? Also, the driver had me sign his screen on the doorstep before I'd even got the box indoors. I didn't sign to say it was fine, I signed to say I'd got it. A friend says if it says signed clear I've got no claim. Is that right? Do I get the replacement or not?

events.body: Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Wednesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

The lamps arrived today. The box had a band of brown Hartwold Arc tape round one end and the corner under it is crushed in. One lamp base is cracked right through. Photos are uploaded to the order. I'd like a replacement please.

Damage report for DL-3942 (TG-6617, pair of ceramic table lamps): recipient reports a crushed carton corner under a carrier tape band and one lamp base cracked through. Photos are on the order thread. Please register it and tell me what you need.

Logged as DMG-7592. Before we assess we need the carrier's condition record for DL-3942. If the carrier's records don't agree with each other or with the customer, send us all of it as it stands and we take it up with Hartwold Arc. Don't try to reconcile it for us. No decision on a replacement until then.
Please send any condition or exception record held for DL-3942 between hub arrival and delivery on 28 Apr.
Route plan for depot CT-2 published for Monday. 21 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.
DL-3942: hub exception 27 Apr 22:14, 'carton corner damage, retaped, contents not inspected'. Retape band applied. Forwarded for delivery as normal.
Driver handover note DL-3942, 28 Apr 13:32: 'delivered good condition, customer signed clear, no damage noted'. Signature on handset.
My parcel DL-80601 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

Any news? Also, the driver had me sign his screen on the doorstep before I'd even got the box indoors. I didn't sign to say it was fine, I signed to say I'd got it. A friend says if it says signed clear I've got no claim. Is that right? Do I get the replacement or not?

acceptable_actions.summary: Send Damage intake both carrier records as they stand (hub exception 27 Apr, retaped; driver note 28 Apr, good condition, signed clear) with the recipient's account of the signature, under DMG-7592, for their assessment.

must: Passes on both carrier records without reconciling them: the hub exception of 27 Apr 22:14 (carton corner damage, retaped, contents not inspected) and the driver handover note of 28 Apr 13:32 (delivered good condition, customer signed clear)
Includes the recipient's statement that she signed on the doorstep before opening the box, to acknowledge receipt only
References DMG-7592 and asks Damage intake to assess and say what the recipient should be told
must_not: Tells the recipient a replacement is approved, on its way or likely
Tells the recipient that signing clear means she has no claim, or that the signature does not matter
States that the damage happened at the hub or that the carrier is liable
States that the driver's note is false or that the driver ignored visible damage
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DMG-7592, DL-3942 (TG-6617): the carrier's condition records as received, which do not agree with each other. Destination depot: hub exception 27 Apr 22:14, 'carton corner damage, retaped, contents not inspected', retape band applied, forwarded for delivery as normal. Dispatch: driver handover note 28 Apr 13:32, 'delivered good condition, customer signed clear, no damage noted', signature on handset. The recipient, Florian Quarrie, reports a crushed corner under a band of brown carrier tape and one lamp base cracked through, with photos on the order. She adds that she signed the handset on the doorstep before taking the box indoors, to acknowledge receipt and not condition, and asks whether a 'signed clear' note affects her claim. I have not reconciled these or told her anything about the outcome. Please assess and tell me what she should be told.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-108: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
